STEP 1 - Scene: A cafeteria-style lunch of Caesar salad (romaine, croutons, shaved parmesan, creamy dressing) and a slice of cheese pizza.

STEP 2 - Vessel: A square white dinner plate, about 26 cm across. I'll treat its usable area as about 600 cm² (a square plate has more area than a round one of the same width).

STEP 3 - Items:
- Romaine lettuce dressed with Caesar dressing
- Croutons
- Shaved parmesan
- Cheese pizza slice (rectangular, partly cut off at the edge of the photo)

STEP 4 - Area (food covers about 50% of the plate):
- Salad: about 30% of the plate, or 180 cm². Within that, croutons take about 2% and parmesan about 1%.
- Pizza: about 20%, or 120 cm². Part of the slice is cut off at the edge, so I'll count the full slice as about 140 cm².

STEP 5 - Volume:
- Salad: 180 cm² × 3 cm = 540 ml
- Pizza: 140 cm² × 1.2 cm = 168 ml

STEP 6 - Grams:
- Salad with dressing: 540 ml × 0.18 = about 97 g. Of that, about 20 g is dressing, leaving about 77 g of greens.
- Croutons: about 10 g
- Parmesan: about 6 g
- Pizza: 168 ml × 0.7 = about 118 g (density reduced because the crust is airy bread)

STEP 7 - Energy:
- Romaine: 77 g × 17 kcal/100 g = 13 kcal
- Caesar dressing: 20 g × 450 kcal/100 g = 90 kcal
- Croutons: 10 g × 410 kcal/100 g = 41 kcal
- Parmesan: 6 g × 420 kcal/100 g = 25 kcal
- Pizza: 118 g × 266 kcal/100 g = 314 kcal

STEP 8 - Sanity check: The total is about 231 g and 483 kcal. That is reasonable for one pizza slice plus a side Caesar salad.
